_note: A floor of the Cairnworks. **One plate, one lane.** The thing on it has every defence at the cap but one, so the floor is answered by the lane it has left open rather than by a bigger number — and the floor's own pool holds that same creature, which is what makes it farmable once the plate is clear. That is the existing shape rather than a new one: eight of the nine boss creatures in this game already stand in a region pool, and here it is on purpose. **Floored with `road`**, like every other dungeon: a floor whose walk costs more than its fight is a corridor with a toll on it.

places.name: the way further down
places.shut: The hatch is under whatever is standing on the plate, and it is standing on it.

regions.name: the Cairnworks
regions._note: **A pool of one, which is the whole of how a floor is farmed.** `draw_enemy` weights a pool by `(max + 1 - rating)`, so the hardest member is the rarest — and a floor whose pool held its boss beside three ordinary creatures dealt that boss about one time in a hundred, which put its drop hundreds of wins away. `a_set_is_a_few_hours_and_not_a_lifetime` said so, in the band it has held since M9. One member has no weighting to get wrong: the room has one thing in it, meeting it again is the farm, and that is what was asked for.
